summary_en: Company shifts from fixed 2030 numerical targets to capital-efficiency and value-creation metrics. Maintains ROE target above 9% and capital cost spread of +3–5%, targeting PBR improvement from current 0.7–0.9x. Six integrated capitals (financial, human, intellectual, manufacturing, social/relational, natural) to be optimized cyclically to exceed cost of capital.
title_en: Initiatives toward realizing management focused on capital cost and share price (including repositioning of long-term vision)
translation_en_brief:
E・J Holdings announced a strategic shift in capital allocation and long-term management philosophy. The company acknowledged that PBR has remained below 1.0x (ranging 0.7–0.9x) over the past five years, while ROE has stayed above 9% and equity spread (ROE minus cost of capital) at +3–5%, though trending lower recently.

Instead of adhering to fixed 2030 numerical targets (sales ¥50B, operating profit ¥6B, net income ¥4B), the company will prioritize capital efficiency and value creation metrics. The company will continue emphasizing ROE improvement and cost-of-capital spread while pursuing PBR recovery through enhanced asset efficiency, stronger cash generation, balanced capital policy (growth investment and shareholder returns), and disciplined capital allocation.

The long-term vision "E・J-Vision2030" will be treated as a "waypoint" rather than an endpoint. Going forward, the company will integrate and cyclically strengthen six capitals—financial, human, intellectual, manufacturing, social/relational, and natural—rather than optimizing them individually. This integrated approach is intended to drive higher value creation and returns exceeding the cost of capital.
